chunks: And from him, from 'Abdillah ibn Nahik, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from 'Abd al-Karim ibn Hassan, who said:

I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What is said, that the Ziyarah of the grave of Abu 'Abdillah al-Husayn (peace be upon him) equals one Hajj and one 'Umrah?' He replied: 'Verily, Hajj and 'Umrah are here (in Makkah). And if a man desired Hajj but was not able (to go), and he came here (to the grave), Allah would write for him a Hajj. And if a man desired 'Umrah but was not able (to go), and he came here, Allah would write for him an 'Umrah.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward of visiting Imam Husayn's grave compared to's grave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) clarifies that the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) serves as a spiritual substitute for Hajj and 'Umrah specifically for those who desire to perform them but are physically or financially unable to travel to Makkah. This distinction highlights the concept of *ziyarah* as a compensatory act of worship (*ibadah*) rather than a replacement for the obligatory pilgrimage itself, a nuance often discussed in Shia fiqh regarding the conditions of validity.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 2. Ja’far ibn Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn ‘Ubaydillāh ibn Mūsā ibn Ja’far narrated to me from ‘Abdillāh ibn Nahīk, from Ibn Abī ‘Umayr, from Hishām ibn Ḥakam, from ‘Abdil Karīm ibn Ḥassān, who said:

I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)), “What does it mean when it is said that going to the Ziyārah of the grave of Abī ‘Abdillāh Al-Ḥusain (a.s.) is equal to performing Hajj and ‘Umrah?” Imam (a.s.) replied: Verily Hajj and ‘Umrah can only be performed here (in Makkah). However, if one decides to go to Hajj but does not have the means (to do so) and goes to Ḥusain (a.s.) instead, Allāh will register a Hajj for him. (Similarly) if one decides to perform an ‘Umrah but does not have the means (to do so) and goes to Ḥusain (a.s.) instead, Allāh will register an ‘Umrah for him.
